landmarks.name: Obo National Park
landmarks.writeup: A protected rainforest area known for its biodiversity and endemic species.

landmarks.name: Roça Sundy
landmarks.writeup: A historic plantation site linked to the abolition of slavery in the islands.

wiki.extract: Sundy is a settlement in the northwestern part of Príncipe Island in São Tomé and Príncipe. Its population is 416. Sundy lies 5 km northwest of the island capital of Santo António. In 1822 the first cocoa plantation of the whole archipelago was established in Sundy. Several buildings of this plantation have been preserved.

landmarks.name: São Sebastião Museum
landmarks.writeup: A cultural museum housed in a former fortress showcasing local history.

wiki.extract: São Tomé is the capital and largest city of the Central African island country of São Tomé and Príncipe. Its name is Portuguese for "Saint Thomas". Founded in the 15th century, it is one of Africa's oldest colonial cities.

cultural_events.name: São Tomé and Príncipe Independence Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on July 12, marking independence from Portugal in 1975 with parades and cultural performances.

cultural_events.name: Festival of the Black Christ
cultural_events.writeup: A religious and cultural festival featuring processions and traditional music.

food_writeup: The cuisine features seafood, tropical fruits, and dishes like calulu, a stew made with fish or meat, vegetables, and palm oil, reflecting Portuguese and African influences.
brief_history: Discovered by Portuguese explorers in the late 15th century, the islands were uninhabited before colonization. They became a key site for sugar and cocoa plantations using enslaved labor. Sao Tome and Principe gained independence from Portugal in 1975 and has since developed as a small island nation with a focus on agriculture and eco-tourism.

important_people.name: Miguel Trovoada
important_people.description: Former President and key figure in independence.

current_conflicts: No significant internal or external conflicts reported.
